chunks: And a group informed me, from Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, who said: A group of my associates, who were residents of our town in Baghdad in the year the Qarmatians raided the pilgrims, which was the year of the falling of the stars, narrated that my father, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him, seeking permission to go out for Hajj.

The reply came: 'Do not go out in this year.' He repeated and said: 'It is an obligatory vow; is it permissible for me to stay behind?' The reply came: 'If you must, then be in the last caravan.' So he was in the last caravan and saved himself, while those who preceded him in the other caravans were killed.

key_terms.الشَّيْخُ أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a prominent deputy of the Imam
key_terms.النَّذْرُ: Vow, a pledge to perform an act of worship
key_terms.الْقَرْمَطُونَ: Qarmatians, a sect known for raiding pilgrims

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s) regarding Hajj during the Qarmatian raid on pilgrims?
ai.summary: This epistle from the Minor Occultation period highlights the strategic wisdom of the Imam through his deputy, Shaykh al-Ruh, in mitigating the specific danger posed by the Qarmatians' raid on pilgrims. The narrative illustrates the principle of *taqiyya* and practical prudence, where delaying the pilgrimage to join the final caravan ensured the father's safety while earlier groups suffered casualties, serving as a historical validation of the Imam's guidance during times of political instability.
